title: Choose the portfolio's new visual world
question: The roll assigned Passport / Official Dossier for the redesign. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Passport / Official Dossier
options.lineage: the official passport data page and its stamped visa pages
options.thesis: Every real, checkable fact — project, employer, skill — reads like a verified entry, stamped and dated, not asserted.
options.viewport: A data page: ruled photo-ID box holding the headshot at left, name/role/location set as ruled fields at right, a masthead cover strip above, an availability stamp strip below.
options.risk: Reads bureaucratic and cold if the ink stays literal instead of warm — needs confident color and real warmth in the copy so it reads as credibility, not paperwork.

raised.raise: The hero commits to one oversized, fully-held statement instead of splitting attention across several small elements.
Accumulated stamps and page wear become literal proof of a real career timeline, not decoration.
Language and theme toggles synchronize as one bilingual-document state change instead of two independent switches.
Each section change gets its own named transition beat (a page-turn/stamp-press), not one uniform fade repeated everywhere.

options.label: Systems Architecture Diagram
options.lineage: the whiteboard system-design diagram engineers draw daily
options.thesis: The page itself is a system diagram — Hero, Work, Experience, Skills, and Contact as connected service nodes a recruiter reads the way they'd read a design doc.
options.viewport: A legend rail at left naming every node; a central canvas of connected boxes (Work, Experience, Skills, Contact) wired to a Hero root node; a status/data-flow strip beneath.
options.risk: Diagram-as-navigation is a familiar move within developer personal sites specifically — the safer, more expected read inside this exact audience, even though it's rare in hiring-facing portfolios broadly.

regions.label: connected system diagram (Hero root → Work/Experience/Skills/Contact nodes)

options.label: Particle Detector Event Display
options.lineage: collider event displays, concentric detector rings around one frozen collision
options.thesis: Career evidence reads like a detected event: concentric rings of Work, Experience, and Skills traced outward from one center.
options.case: Fuses well on identification — the applied-physics background is real and specific to this person — but concentric rings ask more domain literacy than a general hiring audience brings; competitive, not a clean win on clarity.
options.risk: A non-physicist recruiter may not parse concentric rings quickly without labels doing real work — clarity depends entirely on legible in-context labeling.

options.label: Swiss Grid Poster Wall
options.lineage: Swiss International Style concert-poster series, one modular grid across the set
options.thesis: One disciplined module governs every section — objective, flush-left, instantly scannable, nothing decorative.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the grid disciplines every section into equally scannable units, matching ‘fast to evaluate’ directly; loses narrowly on narrative specificity to the actual moment of being evaluated for a role.
options.risk: Reads as generic 'clean corporate' if the grid isn't pushed to genuine density and rigor — easy to under-commit into blandness.

options.label: WebGL Shader Portal
options.lineage: full-bleed GPU shader scenes behind thin floating type
options.case: Fuses poorly: a recruiter needs fast, scannable evidence, not an immersive shader environment to navigate through, and the motion/performance risk works against 'fast to evaluate'.
options.kept: One oversized, fully committed hero moment.

options.label: Hand-Processed Film
options.lineage: 16mm film strip with scratches, chemical bloom, and light leaks
options.case: Fuses poorly: no tie to verifiable technical evidence, and visual noise works against legibility for a hiring evaluation.
options.kept: Material wear as literal proof of history — accumulated marks recording real time passing.

options.label: Rain-Dark Cityscape
options.lineage: a skyline passing from blue hour into rain-dark night
options.case: Fuses poorly: mood-first and thematically distant from proving technical competence to a hiring audience; over-engineered for the actual task.
options.kept: Layered states synchronized on one shared axis instead of two independent toggles.

options.label: Saturday-Morning Title Card
options.lineage: cel-paint cartoon title cards with a starburst logotype
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful consumer-entertainment tone directly undercuts credibility for a full-time hiring decision.
options.kept: A distinct transition beat between sections, not one uniform fade repeated everywhere.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean modern developer-portfolio template — hairlines, serif display, cream ground — executed at full craft, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement this category always ships: left-aligned hero, portrait right, hairline-divided list sections below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design — this is the site's current look, offered straight rather than replaced.
